edges.description: Increased maternal UBE3A dosage contributes to neuronal hyperexcitability in patient-derived neurons.
The duplicated GABAA-receptor gene cluster is associated with the characteristic beta EEG signal, although the molecular route remains unresolved.
Patient-derived Dup15q neurons show altered sodium-current density and inactivation kinetics downstream of the chromosomal duplication.
The maternal duplication causes developmental impairment through cellular intermediates that remain incompletely resolved.
Early motor-milestone delay is a core consequence of the maternal duplication, with unresolved cellular intermediates.
Gait abnormalities accompany the motor phenotype, but the contributions of hypotonia, cognition, medication, and specific neural circuits remain unresolved.
Speech and language development is impaired through unresolved neurodevelopmental mechanisms.
Cognitive impairment follows the maternal dosage increase through unresolved developmental mechanisms.
Autistic behavior is strongly associated with the maternal duplication, but no single-gene or single-circuit route is established.
Central hypotonia is an early manifestation with incompletely resolved cellular intermediates.
Feeding difficulties occur in infancy, including the newborn period in idic15, with unresolved links to hypotonia and other developmental abnormalities.
Growth delay is reported in idic15, but its relationship to the duplicated interval, feeding difficulties, and other clinical factors is unresolved.
Behavioral abnormalities accompany the neurodevelopmental phenotype, but the causal cellular route is unresolved.
Psychosis is a rare neuropsychiatric manifestation with unresolved mechanistic intermediates.
Gastrointestinal dysfunction is common, but its relationship to the duplicated interval has not been resolved in humans.
Gastroesophageal reflux is a recurrent gastrointestinal manifestation with unresolved mechanistic intermediates.
Facial dysmorphic features are usually subtle and arise through unresolved developmental mechanisms.
Human sleep EEG shows abnormal NREM architecture, but its causal relation to individual duplicated genes and beta oscillations is unresolved.
Increased excitability in cultured patient-derived neurons is a plausible substrate for epilepsy, but the intervening human network mechanisms have not been demonstrated.
Dysfunctional sodium-channel inactivation is linked to other epilepsies, but the route from the cultured-cell phenotype to human Dup15q seizures is unresolved.
Epileptogenic network dysfunction manifests as seizures of variable severity.
Infantile spasms are an early epilepsy presentation, especially in the idic15 subtype.
SUDEP is a serious complication reported particularly with the more epilepsy-prone idic15 subtype.

nodes.description: Epilepsy treatment is tailored to seizure type and syndrome. Family-survey and retrospective multicenter data associate broad-spectrum antiseizure medications, oxcarbazepine, and valproate with responses in subsets; the survey also found ACTH more effective than vigabatrin for infantile spasms. These nonrandomized findings do not establish a universal hierarchy.

nodes.description: Patient-derived Dup15q neurons show hyperexcitability that is largely prevented by normalizing UBE3A dosage. UBE3A overexpression alone did not reproduce all synaptic phenotypes, indicating that it is necessary for many observed cellular abnormalities but is not sufficient to explain Dup15q.

evidence.reference_title: The role of UBE3A in the autism and epilepsy-related Dup15q syndrome using patient-derived, CRISPR-corrected neurons.
evidence.snippet: Dup15q neurons exhibited hyperexcitability compared with control neurons, and this phenotype was generally prevented by normalizing UBE3A levels using antisense oligonucleotides. Overexpression of UBE3A resulted in a profile similar to that of Dup15q neurons except for synaptic phenotypes. These results indicate that UBE3A overexpression is necessary for most Dup15q cellular phenotypes but also suggest a role for other genes in the duplicated region.
